answer:
No. Lisinopril was stopped on September 22, 2025, because of a dry cough, and losartan 50 mg daily replaced it. Your Fernhill Family Clinic visit plan from that day and the Kestrel Harbor summary from March 2026 both show it as stopped, and the July 2026 pharmacy record does not list it. A dry cough from lisinopril is recorded as an intolerance. The app is most likely showing an older copy of your records, because the Kestrel Harbor records from spring and summer 2025 still list lisinopril as active. Please don't restart it. Ask the app to refresh its records, and tell Dr. Marsh that the old entry is still showing.

While checking this, I found a more serious problem. The hospital stopped hydrochlorothiazide on March 5, 2026, because your sodium was low (123 at the time). But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2, 2026, with two refills left, and a medication list from May 14, 2026 still shows you taking it. The hospital told you to stop it, so please check with Dr. Marsh or the pharmacy soon. Your sodium was still slightly low (134) on June 15, 2026.

The hospital also asked for a repeat thyroid test (TSH and free T4) 6 to 8 weeks after discharge. I can't find one in your records.

knowledge.says: A dry cough is a known side effect of lisinopril, which belongs to the ACE inhibitor class. It usually improves within weeks of stopping. It is an intolerance rather than an allergy, and the usual alternative is an ARB such as losartan.
knowledge.guideline: ACC/AHA 2017 high blood pressure guideline: an ARB is the alternative when an ACE inhibitor causes cough
